Hiring Team Adolescent Wellness Academy
Re: Creative Group Facilitator, Adolescent Mental Health

Dear Hiring Team,
I recently came across your Creative Group Facilitator opening and wanted to introduce myself. I understand the position may have been filled, but I would welcome consideration for this or future opportunities with Adolescent Wellness Academy.

My background brings together adolescent behavioral health support, recovery group facilitation, visual arts education, and fitness and wellness programming. 

At Family Center for Recovery, I supported adolescents and adults in structured treatment settings. At Futures Recovery Healthcare, I facilitated recovery support groups and helped alumni connect with resources and coping strategies. More recently, as an art teacher, I have designed creative activities that encourage confidence, expression, and engagement.

I am especially drawn to opportunities to help young people strengthen self-esteem and positive self-talk through art, movement, drama-inspired expression, and mindfulness. My approach values practical DBT-informed skills and creative activities as complements to the work of licensed treatment professionals.

I would be grateful for the opportunity to discuss how my experience might support your programming. I have attached my resume for your consideration. 

Thank you for your time.

Warm regards, Jennifer Winston

Sylvia De La Fuentes
Fresno, CA 93723 | The1stroundpick@gmail.com | 559-721-3608
 

Dear Adolescent Wellness Academy Team,
When I think about Support and the importance of support while someone fights to transform their life in addiction and mental health care, I know firsthand that when someone reaches out for support, that first human connection can change everything. I thrive in those exact moments of uncertainty, bringing warmth, clarity, and genuine advocacy to help individuals take that brave first step toward recovery.

In my current role as Lead Program Aide at Beloved Survivors, I manage client intakes, assess support needs, and track service referrals to connect individuals with vital community resources. Whether I am guiding someone through housing options or navigating employment applications, my priority is always making sure no one falls through the cracks. I understand that intake is not just about processing information; it is about building instant trust, listening deeply to a person's barriers and motivations, and walking alongside them with unwavering empathy.

My background spans both compassionate healthcare support and fast-paced operational execution. At Aetna as a Medicare Customer Service Representative, I handled high-volume inbound calls and outbound follow-ups, verified eligibility details, and maintained strict HIPAA compliance while supporting members through complex coverage questions. Additionally, my experience managing Salesforce CRM datasets and high-volume workflows at Oriental Motor taught me how to move quickly across multiple live queues, stay organized in a technology-enabled environment, and treat metrics as tools to improve service quality rather than sources of pressure.

I bring a consultative, outcomes-driven mindset combined with a deep, personal commitment to expanding access to high-quality care. I am ready to bring my energy, heart, and organizational ownership to Adolescent Wellness Academy.
 
Warmly,
Sylvia De La Fuentes

candidates.cover_letter:
Dear AWA People & Culture team,

I first came across Adolescent Wellness Academy through a job post. With a bit of research, I found it to be a beloved program that changed many young lives for the better. As a creative professional with a growing interest in psychology and a wish to work with the younger crowd, I made a note to myself: Reach out. With my help as a social media professional, we can share your story, multiply the healing impact and foster deeper connections with the local community.

As a digital storyteller, I have spent the last decade sharpening my tools, working in all facets of content production from concept development to polished delivery with a brand-tailored, mission-aligned strategic foundation. At Little’s Photography, I worked closely with hundreds of high-schoolers as a fine-art senior portrait photographer and photo editor, while producing an extensive promotional video library for the studio’s marketing initiatives. Our promos reached thousands of clients and led to a surge in the sales of photoshoot packages. I produced organic social content for the Columbia College Chicago Student Communications IG feed, and filmed interview-based documentaries that were showcased all across the university campus. With consistent hard-work as a freelancer, one of my long-time remote clients Emel Onur now has 47,500+ followers on her YouTube channel, compared to the 50 followers we started our journey with.

More recently, I helped establish an Instagram account that is dear to me. My teenage cousin Kağan has a rare form of epilepsy called Dravet Syndrome. Against all odds, he joined the Turkish national tennis team in the special needs category. My aunt was inspired to share their story, so we can build a community and reach those who can help Kağan access the treatment he needs. In the last 3 months, our engagement surged and we got more than 200,000 views. More importantly, we connected with people in very meaningful ways and networked with a foundation who wants to conduct research to find the right treatment. It makes me very happy to be able to have a positive effect on my family and community in Turkey from thousands of miles away.

What excites me the most about the prospect of joining your team is that I wholeheartedly share the aspiration to provide a safe space for teens, where they feel loved and cared for, so we water the seeds of healing for generations to come. I’d appreciate the chance to discuss how I can contribute to your mission. You can reach me at 561-409-6908 or idilmeric@hotmail.com. Thank you for your time—I look forward to hearing from you.

Warm regards,
Idil Meric

questionnaire.text: What experience do you have supporting adolescents, families, or individuals receiving behavioral health services?
questionnaire.response:
In 1998 I worked for a year in the Department of Psychiatry assisting with HIV/AIDS patients. I sat in meetings and took notes as the Psychiatrist conducted group sessions with patients.. I ran to get tissues, water or just hold patients who were emotionally distressed and needed a shoulder.  Later in 2005, I moved to Florida and had my daughter. I waited for my son and daughter to be eligible for preK and kindergarten so I could return to work.   I found work as an ESOL paraprofessional helping High School students from other countries learn to speak English.  During those 9 years I learned not only to help many Spanish speaking students learn English, but how to care for the ones who were emotionally distressed from various personal problems at home, I would accompany them to the social workers office and translate all the problems they were experiencing at home. I realized how much suffering and empathy was needed for my role.  I later left the position to care for my son who had a massive brain tumor and barely survived during the surgery.  As my son, progressed and I was forced to stay home.  I found work on line, which happened to be during COVID. 
   I recently went back to work part time as a Substitute teacher, and still find myself helping students of all ages with a variety of emotional issues.

These qualities are not only essential in our personal lives at home with our families, but when dealing with all people, especially those battling illnesses and obstacles!

I am excited to apply for the Clinic Director position leading the launch of Adolescent Wellness Academy’s first North Carolina clinic. As a licensed clinical social work and case management leader with more than 15 years of experience across behavioral health, healthcare, higher education, and community services, I offer the clinical supervision, operational leadership, and change-management experience needed to build a strong program from the ground up. AWA’s opportunity to create a focused, family-centered PHP/IOP clinic for adolescents is especially compelling to me because it combines direct clinical impact with the chance to shape culture, quality, and sustainable growth from day one.

Throughout my career, I have led complex case coordination, crisis response, care transitions, quality assurance, policy development, talent development, budgeting, and resource allocation. I have also provided clinical supervision and operational management while partnering with healthcare providers, hospital leaders, community agencies, and other stakeholders. These experiences would enable me to recruit and develop clinicians, establish clear clinical and documentation standards, guide level-of-care decisions, and build trusted relationships with families and referral partners across North Carolina.

I would bring a practical, outcomes-focused approach to launch execution: hiring and onboarding a cohesive team; creating a supportive environment for early-career clinicians; establishing reliable crisis, documentation, and quality-review processes; and using assessment findings and utilization trends to strengthen care delivery. My Master of Social Work and ongoing Doctor of Social Work studies in leadership further support my ability to connect evidence-informed clinical practice with disciplined operations and organizational growth.

AWA’s values—Dare to Grow, Contribute to the Whole, Choose Kindness, Spread Optimism, and Deliver Results—reflect how I strive to lead: with accountability, collaboration, compassion, and a clear commitment to excellent outcomes. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my clinical and operational leadership can help AWA launch a high-quality adolescent program and establish a strong foundation for long-term success in North Carolina.
Thank you for your consideration.

Sincerely,
Ty Matthews, LCSW, LISW-CP, DSW (C)

candidates.cover_letter:
Dear Adolescent Wellness Academy Hiring Team,

I am excited to apply for the Bilingual Virtual Program Coordinator position. What drew me to this opportunity is the chance to support adolescents and their families during a time when having consistent, compassionate, and accessible mental health care can make such a meaningful difference.

Throughout my experience in behavioral health, I have found that the work I value most involves supporting children and families while contributing to the teams responsible for their care. As an RBT and Student Analyst, I have worked closely with children and families, assisted with initial assessments and reassessments, contributed to treatment planning, supported parent training, and collaborated with multidisciplinary providers. These experiences have given me a strong understanding of the importance of communication, documentation, and teamwork in behavioral health services.

In addition to my clinical experience, my previous role as a Health Assistant gave me a strong foundation in healthcare administration and remote client support. I worked with clients to verify insurance benefits, reviewed coverage information, assisted with claims and payment-related inquiries, and handled a high volume of calls while communicating with English- and Spanish-speaking families. This experience strengthened my ability to multitask, navigate administrative processes, maintain accurate information, and provide helpful, professional support in a remote setting.

My experience as a Child Protective Investigator also shaped the way I approach family communication. It taught me the importance of listening without judgment, handling sensitive situations with care, and recognizing when concerns need to be communicated or escalated. I believe these skills would be especially valuable when supporting adolescents and families participating in AWA's virtual program.

As a bilingual English and Spanish speaker, I would love the opportunity to help families feel comfortable navigating the admissions process, staying connected with the program, and understanding important updates. I am particularly interested in bringing together my behavioral health and administrative experience in a role that allows me to contribute to the day-to-day operations of a program making a meaningful difference in the lives of adolescents.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my background, experience, and genuine interest in supporting young people could contribute to the AWA team.

Warmly,
Josmari Arroyo

Sincerely,
Terri Setzer

candidates.cover_letter:
My name is Corey Ann, and I’m the founder of Gypsy Jasmine Wellness. I’m a wellness practitioner with a background in yoga, personal training, mindful movement, and holistic wellness. My approach integrates movement, breathwork, somatic practices, fascia release, and mindfulness to support the mind-body connection and promote overall well-being.

Through my work, I aim to create welcoming, accessible experiences that help individuals reduce stress, reconnect with their bodies, improve mobility, cultivate self-awareness, and develop practical tools for navigating life's challenges.

My offerings include yoga, yoga nidra, guided relaxation, somatic movement, breathwork, fascia release, mobility, wellness coaching, and customized workshops and group experiences. I enjoy adapting my approach to meet the unique needs of different populations and environments.

My own journey with chronic pain and recovery has shaped my passion for this work and strengthened my belief in the importance of compassionate, individualized wellness support. I strive to create spaces where people feel supported, empowered, and encouraged to explore their own path toward greater well being.

I would welcome the opportunity to connect, learn more about your organization, and explore how my experience and offerings might complement your existing programs.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I look forward to the possibility of connecting!

Through art instruction and guided creative workshops, I have facilitated activities that incorporate painting, storytelling, imagination, and self-expression to encourage creativity, personal growth, and meaningful engagement.

Sincerely,

Shamaiah Manriquez

Dear Hiring Manager,

I am writing to express my interest in the Therapy position at Adolescent Wellness Academy. As a Registered Clinical Social Work Intern (RCSWI), I am passionate about supporting individuals through life’s challenges and helping them develop the tools and skills necessary to achieve emotional wellness, resilience, and personal growth. I believe my clinical experience, diverse background working with various populations, and dedication to providing compassionate, client-centered care would make me a valuable addition to your team.

In my current role, I provide therapeutic services to youth, adolescents, and adults with a wide range of mental health and behavioral health needs, including PTSD, depression, anxiety, ADHD, autism, and substance use disorders. I utilize evidence-based therapeutic approaches, including Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT), Dialectical Behavior Therapy (DBT), and trauma-informed care, to help clients navigate challenges, strengthen coping skills, regulate emotions, and work toward their individualized treatment goals. I strive to create a safe, supportive, and nonjudgmental therapeutic environment where clients feel heard, respected, and empowered throughout their healing journey.

In addition to my clinical experience, I have worked with diverse and vulnerable populations, including individuals impacted by domestic violence, substance use, homelessness, disabilities, and challenges associated with aging. These experiences have strengthened my ability to approach each individual with empathy, patience, cultural sensitivity, and an understanding of the unique circumstances that influence mental health and overall well-being. I recognize the importance of meeting clients where they are, building trusting therapeutic relationships, and tailoring interventions to their individual needs and strengths.

I am a driven, hardworking, compassionate, and dedicated professional who values collaboration, continued learning, and professional growth. I am committed to helping clients recognize their strengths, overcome barriers, and build healthier, more fulfilling lives. I am particularly interested in the opportunity to contribute my skills and passion to Adolescent Wellness Academy and support the emotional and psychological well-being of the individuals and families served by your organization.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my clinical experience, therapeutic approach, and commitment to quality mental health care align with the needs of your team. I look forward to the possibility of contributing to the important work being done at Adolescent Wellness Academy.

Dear Adolescent Wellness Academy Hiring Team,

I am excited to express my interest in joining the clinical team at Adolescent Wellness Academy. As a Florida Registered Mental Health Counselor Intern (RMHCI) with over 15 years of experience working with adolescents and young adults, I bring a unique combination of clinical training, youth development, experiential education, and a genuine passion for helping young people navigate life's challenges.

My journey into clinical mental health counseling grew naturally from my years working in Jewish education, teen engagement, summer camps, and experiential programming. Throughout these experiences, I discovered that some of the most meaningful growth opportunities happen when young people feel connected, supported, and empowered to explore who they are. This philosophy continues to shape my work as a therapist today.

I earned my Master of Science in Clinical Mental Health Counseling from Lynn University and currently provide individual therapy at Ellie Mental Health. My clinical experience also includes working with adolescents at Family First and with young adults at New Directions for Young Adults, where I facilitated therapeutic groups focused on emotional regulation, interpersonal effectiveness, coping skills, and personal growth. These experiences strengthened my ability to engage clients with diverse clinical needs while balancing therapeutic connection, structured interventions, and individualized treatment goals.

My clinical approach is grounded in Adlerian theory, with an emphasis on belonging, social connection, encouragement, and understanding the patterns that shape how individuals see themselves and the world. I integrate Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT), Dialectical Behavior Therapy (DBT), Motivational Interviewing, and experiential interventions to create meaningful growth opportunities. I particularly enjoy incorporating creativity, active engagement, and play into the therapeutic process, recognizing that traditional talk therapy is not always the most effective way to connect with every adolescent.

What draws me to Adolescent Wellness Academy is your commitment to seeing beyond a teenager's presenting behaviors and recognizing the individual underneath. I strongly believe that adolescents deserve therapeutic spaces where they feel heard, respected, and valued, especially during some of their most challenging moments. Your collaborative, multidisciplinary treatment environment aligns with both my clinical philosophy and my longstanding commitment to supporting young people.

I would welcome the opportunity to bring my clinical skills, extensive experience in youth engagement, and enthusiasm for experiential therapeutic work to your team. Thank you for considering my application. I look forward to the opportunity to discuss how my background and approach could contribute to the meaningful work being done at Adolescent Wellness Academy.

In Community,

Ross Glinkenhouse, MS, Registered Mental Health Counselor Intern

I am so excited to apply for the opportunity to join AWA Academy’s IOP/PHP team working with adolescents. As a therapist who graduated in December 2025, I am eager to continue growing as a clinician in a setting that aligns with something I am truly passionate about: supporting children, adolescents, and their families. Dear Hiring Committee, 

Thank you for taking the time to review my resume and cover letter. I am writing to express my enthusiasm for the opportunity to continue my experience working as a Registered Mental Health Counseling Intern at  Adolescent Wellness Academy. I received a Bachelor of Science in Psychology and am a recent graduate with my Masters in Mental Health Counseling from the University of Miami.

My educational experiences have helped me to build my knowledge and experience for working as a registered mental health counseling intern. I have a strong academic background in psychology, as well as a strong interest in working with children and their families to address mental health challenges at an early age, including Attention Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder, Anxiety, and Depression. Through my recent experiences working as a practicum intern at Nicklaus Children’s Hospital and the Institute for Individual and Family Counseling, I was able to establish a strong foundation in conceptualizing cases, applying interventions and building rapport. 

In my previous experience working at Florida International University’s Summer Treatment Program, I had the opportunity to work directly with children and their families, providing support in areas such as emotional regulation, coping skills, and behavioral management. These experiences have provided a good foundation in implementing therapeutic strategies tailored to the unique needs of young children, as well as solidified my interest in child and adolescent mental health. 

I have a passion for working with programs that help to provide low-cost services for a diverse population, as highlighted in my experience working as a practicum intern at the institute for Individual and Family Counseling. I believe that my strong communication skills and dedication will allow for a wonderful learning experience as I continue my work in the field of mental health counseling.  

I have included my resume and look forward to the possibility of discussing further my qualifications. Please feel welcome to contact me at your earliest convenience. I look forward to hearing from you. 

Respectfully,

Dear Hiring Manager,
I am excited to apply for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position with Adolescent Wellness Academy (AWA) and Principles Recovery Center (PRC). With a Bachelor's degree in Psychology and extensive experience in behavioral health, social services, and care coordination, I have built a career helping individuals and families navigate difficult situations and connect with the services they need. I am passionate about being a compassionate first point of contact and would welcome the opportunity to support clients on their path to recovery and wellness.
Throughout my career, I have conducted assessments, gathered sensitive information, coordinated services, and worked closely with families experiencing mental health, behavioral, and substance use challenges. As a Positive Supports Consultant with the State of Missouri, I regularly communicate with providers, caregivers, and support teams, assess needs, review documentation, and guide individuals toward appropriate resources. These responsibilities require strong communication skills, attention to detail, and the ability to build trust quickly, even during stressful situations.
My previous experience as an Associate Social Services Specialist and Integrated Health Specialist further strengthened my ability to conduct intake interviews, maintain accurate records, coordinate referrals, and support individuals through complex systems of care. I am comfortable discussing sensitive topics, managing confidential information, and maintaining detailed documentation while ensuring a positive experience for those seeking assistance.
In addition to my clinical and social service background, I am highly self-motivated and accustomed to working independently, managing multiple priorities, and utilizing electronic record systems to track information and ensure timely follow-up. Colleagues often describe me as compassionate, organized, and dependable, qualities that align closely with your need for someone who can consistently support families from the initial call through admission.
What attracts me most to this opportunity is the ability to make an immediate impact during a critical moment in someone's life. I understand that reaching out for help can be overwhelming, and I take pride in creating a supportive, welcoming experience while helping individuals and families take the next step toward treatment.
Thank you for your consideration. I look forward to the opportunity to discuss how my experience in behavioral health, case management, and client engagement can contribute to your admissions team.
Sincerely,
Kayla Heintz

candidates.cover_letter:
RE: Program Director, Virtual Intensive Outpatient Program

Dear Hiring Manager,

I am writing to express my interest in the Program Director, Virtual Intensive Outpatient Program position with Adolescent Wellness Academy. With over 20 years of experience in behavioral health, residential services, and program operations, I bring a strong background in leadership, staff development, clinical coordination, and quality improvement. I am excited about the opportunity to contribute my experience to a growing program focused on improving access to mental health services for adolescents and their families.

Throughout my career, I have held progressively responsible positions, including Behavioral Health Program Manager and Coordinator, overseeing daily operations across multiple outpatient services. In these roles, I supervised more than 21 employees, coordinated multidisciplinary teams, monitored program productivity and spending, and supported operational improvements to strengthen service delivery. My experience also includes admissions coordination, community referrals, staff scheduling, documentation oversight, and maintaining compliance with Medicaid, DCF, CARF, and HIPAA requirements.

My professional background has allowed me to develop a strong understanding of the importance of balancing clinical quality with operational efficiency. I recognize that building a successful program requires more than providing services. It involves developing strong referral relationships, supporting staff, monitoring performance, identifying opportunities for growth, and ensuring that individuals and families receive timely, coordinated care.

Although much of my recent clinical and operational experience has focused on adults with mental health and co-occurring substance use disorders, my earlier experience providing behavioral support services has strengthened my understanding of individualized care, family collaboration, and the importance of early intervention. I believe these experiences provide a valuable foundation for supporting Adolescent Wellness Academy's family-centered approach to adolescent treatment.

I have completed all requirements for my Master of Social Work degree through Walden University and am awaiting official degree conferral. I also hold the Certified Behavioral Health Case Manager Supervisor (CBHCMS) credential and have submitted my application for Florida Registered Clinical Social Work Intern registration. These professional milestones reflect my continued commitment to clinical development, ethical practice, and effective behavioral health leadership.

I would welcome the opportunity to bring my leadership experience, operational knowledge, and commitment to quality care to Adolescent Wellness Academy. I am particularly interested in contributing to the continued development of its Virtual IOP through strong team leadership, community partnerships, and a consistent focus on program performance and client outcomes.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I look forward to the opportunity to discuss how my experience and professional goals align with the needs of your organization.

Sincerely,

Michelle Antonia Rivera
CBHCMS
MSW Program Completed

candidates.cover_letter:
Dear Hiring Manager,

I am writing to express my interest in joining your organization. As a Licensed Mental Health Counselor in Florida with over 10 years of experience in behavioral health, I bring a strong background in clinical quality assurance, compliance, clinical leadership, and direct patient care. My experience has provided me with a comprehensive understanding of clinical operations, documentation standards, and the importance of delivering high-quality, compliant behavioral health services.

In my current role as a Clinical Quality and Compliance Specialist at Brave Health, I conduct over 200 clinical audits quarterly, reviewing more than 1,000 clinical records to evaluate medical necessity, diagnostic accuracy, appropriate levels of care, documentation quality, and compliance with payer requirements. I also review the work of licensed and pre-licensed clinicians, provide clinical co-signing, and collaborate with management to identify opportunities for improvement. Additionally, I have trained over 200 clinicians and contributed to the development of training resources, competency assessments, and clinical quality improvement processes.

My previous experience as a Lead Therapist further strengthened my skills in clinical oversight, mentorship, and professional development. Throughout my career, I have also conducted comprehensive behavioral health assessments, evaluated clinical risk, established diagnoses, and developed individualized treatment plans for diverse populations. These experiences have strengthened my ability to evaluate clinical information, make sound decisions, and support both clinicians and organizational objectives.

I am particularly interested in opportunities where I can apply my clinical knowledge, analytical skills, and commitment to quality to support effective behavioral health services. As a bilingual professional fluent in English and Spanish, I also bring the ability to communicate effectively with diverse populations and multidisciplinary teams.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I welcome the opportunity to discuss how my experience and qualifications align with the needs of your organization.

Sincerely,

Melissa Ortega, LMHC

Dear Adolescent Wellness Academy Hiring Team,

I am excited to express my interest in the Operations Manager position with Adolescent Wellness Academy as you prepare to open your first North Carolina clinic. What excites me most about this opportunity is the chance to be part of something that can make a genuine difference in the lives of young people and their families. Throughout my career, I have found the most rewarding part of my work is knowing that what I do has a meaningful impact on someone else's life. That is something I experienced firsthand at Shine Support Services, and it is something I hope to continue in my next role.

At Shine Support Services, I helped build the Supportive Employment Program from the ground up. I operated and developed workflows, internal procedures, training materials, participant resources, and documentation standards to help establish the foundation for daily operations. More importantly, I had the opportunity to work directly with individuals with intellectual and developmental disabilities, support their goals, and build relationships with their families and community partners. I loved being able to see the difference that consistent support and encouragement could make in someone's confidence, independence, and everyday life. I taught a coping skills class that incorporated Dialectical Behavior Therapy (DBT) practices, giving participants the opportunity to learn and practice healthy coping strategies. Those experiences reminded me that meaningful progress is not always one big milestone. Sometimes it is the smaller moments of growth that make the work so worthwhile.

I also bring leadership and operational experience from Graphic Components, where I led the photopolymer department before being promoted to Project Manager. I coordinated departmental workflow, monitored quality, addressed production challenges, developed procedures and training documentation, and cross-trained employees and prospective hires. This experience strengthened my ability to organize competing priorities, support a team, solve problems, and create systems that help people do their jobs effectively.

My experience working with young people also extends to YPATC, a youth performing arts program in Florida, where my responsibilities ranged from scheduling appointments to teaching theater to children. I enjoyed being part of an environment where I could contribute both behind the scenes and directly to the experiences of young people. I have pursued the 40-hour Registered Behavior Technician (RBT) training coursework, further developing my understanding of behavioral support and different learning and support needs.

What draws me to AWA is the opportunity to bring these experiences together in a setting where the work has such an important purpose. I understand that a successful program depends on more than the services being offered. It also takes thoughtful organization, dependable staff, clear communication, consistent routines, and an environment where young people and their families feel supported. I would be excited to help build that foundation for AWA's North Carolina clinic.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my experience, leadership, and passion for meaningful work could contribute to AWA's founding North Carolina team.

Sincerely,

Erica R. Warriner

Dear Hiring Manager,

I am writing to express my sincere interest in the Admissions Counselor position at Adolescent Wellness Academy. With six years of experience in education as a Teacher's Assistant and Guidance Counselor, along with over five years of experience in healthcare, including mental health and substance use services, I bring a diverse professional background and a genuine passion for helping adolescents and families navigate life's challenges.

Throughout my career, I have developed a strong ability to build meaningful connections with individuals from all walks of life. My experience has taught me that effective guidance begins with understanding, compassion, and the ability to meet people where they are without judgment. Whether working with students, patients, or families, I believe every individual deserves to feel respected, heard, and valued. I approach every interaction with the understanding that I am not above the person seeking support; I am there to walk alongside them, offer guidance, and help them recognize their own potential.

My background in mental health and substance use services has further strengthened my ability to communicate with empathy, navigate sensitive situations, and establish trust with individuals experiencing vulnerable moments in their lives. My own personal experiences with loss and adversity have also shaped my perspective, deepening my appreciation for resilience, compassion, and the importance of having someone who genuinely believes in you. These experiences have reinforced my commitment to treating every individual with dignity rather than defining them by their circumstances.

My colleagues would describe me as ambitious, focused, reliable, and grounding. I take pride in my ability to bridge the gap between professionalism and relatability, creating connections that allow people to feel comfortable, supported, and understood. I believe my combined experience in education, healthcare, mental health, and substance use services gives me a unique perspective that aligns with the mission of supporting adolescents and their families through important and sometimes difficult transitions.

I am particularly drawn to Adolescent Wellness Academy because I value the opportunity to be part of an organization that prioritizes adolescent wellness, personal growth, and individualized support. I would be honored to bring my professional experience, personal perspective, and genuine dedication to helping others to your admissions team.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I welcome the opportunity to discuss how my experience, compassion, and commitment to serving others would make me a valuable addition to Adolescent Wellness Academy.

Sincerely,

Amanda Nieves-Rodriguez

candidates.cover_letter:
Dear Hiring Manager,

I am excited to apply for the Creative Group Facilitator – Adolescent Mental Health position. As a bilingual behavioral health professional and Marriage and Family Therapy graduate student at Nova Southeastern University, I am passionate about supporting individuals through meaningful, engaging, and creative therapeutic experiences. I am especially interested in this opportunity because it combines mental health support with creative approaches that encourage self-expression, connection, and personal growth.

I currently work as a Recovery Coach at Monte Nido, where I support clients in a structured eating disorder treatment setting. In addition, I am completing my clinical practicum within the PHP/IOP program, where I have gained experience working alongside multidisciplinary treatment teams and supporting clients through various stages of recovery. My responsibilities include providing emotional support, building therapeutic rapport, observing and documenting client interactions, and assisting with daily programming.

I also have experience developing and facilitating therapeutic group activities focused on topics such as body image, boundaries, self-expression, emotional support, and personal growth. I enjoy creating interactive experiences that allow clients to participate, reflect, and connect with themselves and others in ways that feel approachable and meaningful. My graduate education has further strengthened my understanding of mental health, family dynamics, and the importance of meeting clients where they are.

As someone who is bilingual in English and Spanish, I value creating an inclusive and supportive environment where individuals feel comfortable expressing themselves. I would love the opportunity to bring my creativity, clinical experience, and passion for working in behavioral health to your team.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I look forward to the opportunity to discuss how my background, experience, and enthusiasm for adolescent mental health could contribute to your organization.

Sincerely,
Gabriela Perez
